prompt:
You describe a photo or rendering from an electronics datasheet for an engineer who cannot see it.

Cover, in this order:
1. What object is shown and from which side.
2. Every visible marking: labels, part numbers, logos, connectors, pin markings.
3. Dimensions or scale, if shown.

Figure type: photo or rendering
Section: 8 Handling of reels > 8.2 Introduction into production
Caption: Figure 20: Stacking of reels
Text inside the figure (read from this image by a specialised OCR model; use these spellings): Correct Storage. | Wrong Storage.
Text that mentions the figure: When reels are to be stored horizontally, they must be ordered in a stack with at most 4 reels per stack (see images below).

Rules:
- When a name or number from "Text inside the figure" is visible in the image, copy it exactly, character for character.
- Never invent a value, name, pin, unit or connection. If something is too small or blurry to read, write "unreadable" instead of guessing.
- Describe only what this image shows. Do not explain general theory or add advice.
- Mention each item once. Stop when everything is covered.
- Plain text only: no Markdown headings, tables or bold. Short paragraphs and "- " lists are fine.
- Start directly with what the figure is (for example "Block diagram of ..."), not with "The image shows".

answer.text:
Photo of two views of a reel storage setup.

Top view: A black plastic tray containing a single reel of components. The reel has a paper label affixed to it. To the right of the tray, there is a green checkmark followed by the text "Correct Storage.".

Bottom view: A black plastic tray containing a stack of three reels of components. The top reel has a paper label. The middle and bottom reels also have paper labels. A red arrow points to the stack of reels. To the right of the tray, there is a red 'X' followed by the text "Wrong Storage.".

No dimensions or scale are shown.
